messages.subject: heat map
parts:
Hi,
I have a CSV file...
The first column stands for a label which repeats altogether many times in the file. The other columns are just real values.
I want to create a heat map such that the heat map is separated into chunks according to the first column, and then all
rows which are agglomerated together according to the first column (appear one below the other in the heatmap) will
have a label on the y axis telling the cluster name.
Is that possible?

I got close to that using the following

library(ggplot2);
A <- read.csv("data.csv");
A.m <- melt(A);
A.m <- ddply(A.m, .(variable), transform, rescale=rescale(value));
(p<-ggplot(A.m, aes(variable, Name)) + geom_tile(aes(fill =rescale), colour="white") + scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "steelblue"));

but for some reason all rows with the same column are made into one row.

Putting some distinction between the different clusters (i.e. a line in the heat map or something like that) would actually be nice, but it is not necessary, as long as one can tell when the heatmap moves to the next cluster by the label on the y axis.
Any clue would be appreciated.

Thanks!
